title: I Let the Indoor-Cycling Bike Reservation Catch the Instructor's Friend

parts.text: I tapped bike 9 at 5:58 a.m. and instructor Voss's friend was already clipped in on my app hold. The screen said: RESERVE THE BIKE. NO FLOOR SAVES. END ON THE BEEP. I was thirty, member, holding a phone that listed 9. Voss shrugged. "Friends are the room." I photographed the screen, the hold, and the friend's shoes on my pedals. Then I asked for the bike log. At 6:03 the front desk pinged why Voss's name was on a floor save. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Front desk can see Voss's friend clipped into bike 9 during my reservation.

social.video_title: The instructor's friend clipped into my reserved bike — Part 1/2
social.description: Indoor cycling, an app hold, shoes on my pedals. I logged the save. Would you have asked the desk?

parts.text: Voss called it energy until the desk asked for the still. I printed the log, the screen, and the photo. The friend unclipped. Voss ran reserves through the app like everyone else and told the next instructor energy was always about optics. Optics is a word instructors use when an app exists. Reservation now has a second line: FRIENDS ARE NOT THE ROOM. I keep bike 9. Voss brown-bags the jokes. The studio finally looks like a hold, not a favor. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Friends are not the room — Part 2/2
social.description: Bike log, unclipped shoes, and a second line. Was energy ever my hold?
